current_status.to: Active as of 2026-09-23. Sierra County Commissioners unanimously amended and adopted Resolution No. 2026-51 at their July 21, 2026 meeting, imposing an 18-month moratorium on new data centers in the county (through approximately 2028-01-21). As of September 3, 2026, New Mexico Commissioner of Public Lands Stephanie Garcia Richard publicly stated the moratorium also applies to the Spaceport America property (on state trust land) and that she would not approve a proposed Aetherion/Green Data sublease there while it remains in force, and Sierra County Commissioner Sandy Jones told the Albuquerque Journal (reporting published in early September 2026) he would not support efforts to amend or narrow the moratorium despite a developer's lobbying. No rescission, amendment, or replacement was found in sources reviewed through 2026-09-23.
current_status.reason: Resolves the prior VERIFY marker using independent news corroboration and the county clerk's own resolutions index, and adds subsequent developments (the State Land Office's September 3 confirmation that the moratorium binds Spaceport America, and the county's continued resistance to a developer-sought amendment) that establish the moratorium remains in force and unchanged.

new_candidates.date_enacted: Reported adopted 'late last month' (late August 2026) per CPR.org's September 3, 2026 article; a public hearing on the proposed ordinance was held August 11, 2026 and the county's own public notice states the Board of Commissioners could consider adoption at its August 25, 2026 meeting.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Ordinance No. 2026-02 (Colfax County), 'An Ordinance for a Data Center Moratorium,' prohibiting the establishment or expansion of any data center in unincorporated areas of the county and putting municipalities within the county on notice that the county opposes data centers in incorporated areas as well; public hearing held August 11, 2026 per the county's official notice, adoption considered at the August 25, 2026 commission meeting.
new_candidates.trigger: Concern over water use during a severe/extreme drought affecting the county, plus concerns about energy use, heat, and noise; came after the City of Raton's since-expired memorandum of understanding with a data-center developer (Atterix LLC) drew controversy.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23. Colfax County Commissioners unanimously adopted Ordinance No. 2026-02, a one-year moratorium on establishing or expanding data centers in unincorporated areas of the county, at their August 25, 2026 meeting (per the county's own public notice scheduling that consideration and CPR.org's September 3, 2026 report that the ordinance 'passed unanimously late last month'). The moratorium does not bind municipalities within the county (such as the City of Raton), which could still approve a data center; Raton itself considered but postponed its own moratorium proposal around the same time.
new_candidates.affected_projects: None sited in unincorporated Colfax County; the City of Raton separately had a since-expired memorandum of understanding with Atterix LLC to consider a data center at a former K-Mart site, but that is a municipal, not county, matter and is unaffected by this county ordinance.
new_candidates.outcome: Colfax County Commission unanimously adopted a one-year moratorium on new or expanded data centers in unincorporated county territory.
